samples.summary: Third copy of the limit rule left behind — acceptance criterion "One definition of the limit rule in the repo" is not met. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260815-agent-pool-failover-todo.md:60) requires a single definition, and the diff consolidates ask.mjs + redact.mjs + auth-smoke.mjs, but `metrics.mjs` still hard-codes `/\b(?:session|usage)\s+limit\b/i` as the prose fallback when `outcome.code` is absent. That copy is exactly the pre-widening pattern, so a pre-vocabulary record carrying "You've hit your weekly limit" renders the generic "Not retryable as-is; a human should take a look" advice instead of the "wait for the window" advice — the same misdiagnosis the change exists to remove. It should import `SESSION_LIMIT_RE` from redact.mjs like the other three call sites now do.

Design doc not updated for the changed pool semantics. `docs/design/harness-engineering.md` (the canonical doc for the credential pool, Phase threat-model section) states the pool "replaces it only when that account's window closes" — which is precisely the rule this change reverses: a slot is now also retired on a 401/403 refusal, and the pool-exhausted message no longer means "usage limit". Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline this behavioural change to a documented mechanism should be folded into that existing section (not a new parallel doc). The change instead records the rationale only in code comments and docs/tasks/, leaving the design doc actively wrong about when failover happens.

samples.summary: A 401 classified as `AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL` still does not fail over, so the acceptance criterion "A 401/403 fails over to the next healthy credential" is only partly met. `classifyInfraError` checks `MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE` before the status branch (redact.mjs:390), so a slot whose secret has a stray character/newline yields `code === "AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL"`; `isCredentialRejected` keys on `code` first and returns false, and the status fallback never runs. That is the same class of per-slot fault the new design says the pool should route around (one bad secret among N good ones), yet it still stops the whole job — arguably an under-reach of the chosen abstraction.

samples.summary: The pool module's own contract text now contradicts the caller. token-pool.mjs's header rule 2 says "Switch only on exhaustion" and `isExhausted`'s docblock (line ~152) says a drained pool "means every account's window is closed" — both were true only while `isAccountLimit` was the sole failover trigger. The diff carefully re-words the equivalent prose in ask.mjs ("retired", not "usage limit") but leaves the module that actually owns retirement describing the old rule.

Operator-facing advice still names the window as a "session limit" specifically ("This is an account **session limit**…"), which now covers weekly/daily/monthly windows too. Wording only, but it is the same "name one remedy for two shapes" problem the diff's pool-exhausted rewording was written to avoid.

verdict.reason: The quoted evidence is accurate. scripts/agent/metrics.mjs:878 hard-codes /\b(?:session|usage)\s+limit\b/i — a third, pre-widening copy of the limit rule — while the canonical, widened definition is exported at scripts/agent/redact.mjs:305 and imported by the three consolidated call sites (ask.mjs:32, auth-smoke.mjs:35/51, redact.mjs:393). metrics.mjs already imports from redact.mjs (metrics.mjs:40), so the reuse path exists and is unused. This directly fails the acceptance criterion at docs/tasks/active/20260815-agent-pool-failover-todo.md:60 ("One definition of the limit rule in the repo"), which the task marks complete, and contradicts the plan item at lines 41-42 ("the drift is the fault, not the omission"). The path is reachable, not dead: metrics.mjs:866-877 states in its own comment that the prose fallback serves records written before the closed vocabulary existed ("persisted session logs outlive a deploy"), so such a record carrying a weekly/daily/monthly limit falls to the generic "Not retryable as-is; a human should take a look" branch (metrics.mjs:879-886) — the exact misdiagnosis the change exists to remove. No caller-side guard forces outcome.code to be set for persisted records. Duplication/unmet acceptance criterion is squarely in the design-fit lane and rated major by its rubric.

verdict.reason: The canonical harness design doc still describes the pre-change failover rule and was not updated. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1916-1927 is the credential-pool section (indexed as canonical at docs/design/README.md:161; hunter-usage.md is only the operator guide) and line 1923-1924 states the pool "replaces it only when that account's window closes." The change reverses that: scripts/agent/ask.mjs:600-605 adds isCredentialRejected (AUTH_REJECTED / 401 / 403) and ask.mjs:638-642 makes nextCredential fail over on it, while ask.mjs:686-693 restates the exhausted message as "retired" precisely because a slot is now retired for a closed window OR a refused credential (token-pool.mjs:134-176 tracks the retired set). I searched wide for a counterexample: case-insensitive grep of 401|403|AUTH_REJECTED|isCredentialRejected|weekly|retired inside harness-engineering.md yields only one unrelated hit (:2982), and refused|rejected|expired hits only unrelated topics; grep of token-pool|CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN|nextCredential|pool across all of docs/design/** finds no other agent-harness doc (hunter-usage.md has zero "pool" matches), so no alternate or renamed pool doc exists. The repo's own docs-lens record (.agent-review/docs/summary.md:3) confirms the documentation in this change was the two docs/tasks files only. CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 requires evolving the existing area doc, so the behavioural change to a documented mechanism leaves that doc actively wrong — a design-doc-discipline violation, major under this lens.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present (ask.mjs:602 keys on `code` first; redact.mjs:390 tests MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE before the 401/403 branch at redact.mjs:400), but it is not a design-fit/spec-conformance defect. (1) The issue's plan bullet scopes the work verbatim to what was built: "Add `isCredentialRejected` (`AUTH_REJECTED`, falling back to 401/403) and fail over on it in `nextCredential`" (pool-failover-todo.md:45-46), and ask.mjs:600-605 + ask.mjs:638-642 implement exactly that. (2) The acceptance criterion "A 401/403 fails over to the next healthy credential" (pool-failover-todo.md:56) is met: a real 401/403 classifies as AUTH_REJECTED (redact.mjs:400; asserted redact.test.mjs:161-162, ask.test.mjs:687) and fails over. The live incident text named in the issue ("401 OAuth access token is invalid", :33) does not match MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL_RE, which matches only header-frame phrasing (redact.mjs:347-348). (3) The malformed-credential failure is by construction status-less — "the request never left the client" (redact.mjs:387-389), modelled as `{ status: null }` in redact.test.mjs:160 and driven with no api_error_status in redact.test.mjs:207 / ask.test.mjs:651-659 — so it is not "a 401/403" that the criterion covers. (4) The canonical design doc deliberately separates AUTH_MALFORMED_CREDENTIAL because its remedy is "Fix the whitespace in the secret", not "Rotate the credential" (credential-redaction-todo.md:71, 80-82); extending failover to it is behavior the issue never requested. What remains is the finding's own hedge — "arguably an under-reach of the chosen abstraction" — i.e. a taste/preference argument (minor, never blocking here), plus a predicate-ordering question that is line-level logic owned by the correctness lens, not the design-fit lane. It is in fact already filed there (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:5), so refuting here does not remove the concern from the gate.
